routes.description: Establish that human freedom requires genuinely live alternatives and agent sourcehood, and that deliberative experience, constrained indeterminacy, executive selection, and cumulative self-formation can jointly supply those conditions despite biological and social limits.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if alternative-capable deliberation and agent contribution are necessary for freedom and responsibility, if indeterminism can operate through rather than replace rational selection, and if deterministic proximal agency cannot preserve the required authorship.

motionBridge.description: Show that freedom requires both genuinely available alternatives and an agent-originating contribution that deterministic practical agency cannot supply.

centralBridges.description: Establish that first-person deliberation and practical inquiry present alternatives as genuinely available rather than merely hypothetical.
Explain how constrained neural indeterminacy and executive criteria permit rational selection without reducing choice to either prior determination or randomness.
Show that agents originate action and progressively shape their own characters through repeated alternative-capable choices under inherited constraints.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Establish that neuroscience does not decisively show conscious deliberation to be causally idle or choices to be settled before awareness.
Provide a non-dualist account on which conscious valition, brain-level realization, top-down constraint, and indeterminacy can belong to one agent.

routes.description: Establish that determinism preserves practically important freedom through willing action, consent, proximal causation, character, and responsibility practices, without requiring categorical alternatives or ultimate self-origination.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if meaningful distinctions between choices and nonchoices remain available under determinism, if persons can act through their brains and characters as proximal sources, and if libertarian alternatives or sourcehood add no necessary, workable condition for responsibility.

motionBridge.description: Show that freedom, will, and responsibility retain burden-satisfying practical content under determinism without libertarian alternatives or ultimate sourcehood.

centralBridges.description: Ground freedom in durable distinctions among willing, unwilling, consensual, coerced, chosen, and unchosen conduct.
Show that an embodied person can be the causally effective proximal source of conduct through deliberation and character even when prior conditions determine it.
Explain responsibility through plural, practice-shaped concepts of praise, blame, answerability, and reactive attitudes rather than one libertarian essence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test whether genetics, upbringing, and restricted evaluative criteria leave libertarian agents with the ultimate authorship their account requires.
Require a principled account of when an alternative is genuinely live and how that status explains responsibility across constrained cases.

sections.title: The Required Standard of Human Freedom
sections.rationale: Defines the motion-level dispute between libertarian alternatives and sourcehood on one side and compatibilist willing, choice, and practical agency on the other.

sections.title: Deliberation and Genuine Alternative Possibilities
sections.rationale: Tests whether first-person deliberation and practical inquiry support genuinely open options or can coexist with a determined future understood from a third-person perspective.

sections.title: Indeterminism, Randomness, and Agential Selection
sections.rationale: Addresses whether constrained stochastic variation plus executive criteria can produce rational libertarian choice, or whether probabilistic weighting still fails to confer authorship.

sections.title: Sourcehood, Character, and Formative Constraints
sections.rationale: Compares cumulative libertarian self-formation with compatibilist proximal causation while accounting for the roles of genetics, upbringing, evaluative criteria, and constrained opportunities.

sections.title: Responsibility and Practical Agency Under Determinism
sections.rationale: Examines whether consent, coercion, willing conduct, blame, praise, and reactive attitudes preserve freedom-relevant distinctions without categorical alternatives or ultimate sourcehood.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Ordinary deliberation presents agents as considering genuine alternatives, selecting among them, and acting, which supports libertarian freedom absent a sufficient reason to reject that experience.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Libet-style readiness potentials do not establish that unconscious activity causes conscious decisions or actions, because readiness activity can be dissociated from both deciding and moving.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Indeterminism need not be random or reasonless, because probabilistically constrained variation can be evaluated and selected through deliberative processes as part of libertarian agency.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: When the self is identified with the brain's executive or valitional system, the agent participates in imposing the criteria that constrain and govern indeterminate choice.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Despite biological, social, and environmental limits, agents contribute through repeated choices and learning to reshaping their brains, expanding later options, and realizing themselves over time.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Indeterminate neuronal firing can lack a sufficient determining cause while system-level criterial constraints exert top-down causation, providing a physical mechanism for agential selection.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Freedom operates among alternatives genuinely live for an agent, while severe biological or social constraints can narrow those alternatives and correspondingly reduce moral responsibility by degree.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: Responsibility rests partly on an agent's alternative-capable role in gradually shaping the character from which later settled conduct proceeds, not only on isolated proximal choices.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: Taking deliberative phenomenology and practical causal reasoning seriously supports treating agents as originating sources and their apparent ability to do otherwise as real rather than irrelevant.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: The evolved practical indispensability of conscious deliberation and inquiry supports taking their alternative-possibility structure seriously, including when interpreting the agency of other people.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Compatibilism should identify the important notions of freedom and willing that survive determinism rather than claim to preserve the libertarian conception unchanged.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: On monism or physicalism, a person's brain states are parts of that person, so neural causation does not displace personal agency or establish that the person was not the source.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Even if willing is determined, morally important distinctions between willing and unwilling conduct, including consent, survive and provide substantive content for compatibilist freedom.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: A decision produced by weighted stochastic variation may remain no better than randomness for purposes of authorship when the agent's weighting criteria constrain the possible result.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Genetics and upbringing heavily constrain an agent's evaluative criteria and place much of the possible choice space outside the agent's control, challenging claims of ultimate sourcehood.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: A libertarian model may not deliver the ultimate responsibility commonly expected of it when a restrictive environment prevents an agent from developing access to materially different evaluative criteria.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-01.proposition: An alternatives-based account needs a principled way to determine when an option was genuinely live, particularly in cases where restrictive upbringing appears to exclude alternative evaluative paths.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Freedom and responsibility comprise plural, practice-shaped concepts whose content can be reconstructed through praise, blame, coercion, and reactive attitudes rather than one metaphysical formula.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: Even if determinism were proven, distinctions between choices and nonchoices could remain intelligible, while tension between objective inquiry and first-person deliberation would burden theories of human inquiry generally.
